evidence.reason: The drain_refuse_phase fixture setup acquires resources before the cleanup scope begins: `seed_drain_work(kind)` at line 980 and the detached unrelated child at line 981 run before `cleanup = []` (982) and `try:` (983). Because the `try`/`finally` is only entered after both acquisitions, an exception from `spawn_detached` (or a partial failure inside `seed_drain_work` after it has spawned the seeded child/written run metadata) propagates out of the phase without the cleanup path ever executing, leaving the live child and run metadata behind. The same acquisition-before-scope structure is alleged at 1082-1083 and 1207-1208. This is an ordinary exception-safety defect in the harness's existing intended cleanup behavior, not a request to add approval/protection scope; the smallest fix is to open the cleanup scope before acquiring either fixture and register each resource as soon as it is obtained. No commit in the supplied history moves the setup inside the scope, so it is not fixed; it is not a duplicate and no contract clause retires this concern.
